assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major reorientation of research on inequality through long-run income and wealth measurement, with consequential findings on concentration and taxation.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman form a coherent group linking historical series, tax-record evidence and the measurement of wealth including offshore wealth.
assessment.maturity: The empirical infrastructure and its use across public economics and economic history are mature and highly influential.
uncertainties: Estimates of wealth, especially offshore wealth, depend on imperfect records and modelling choices.
The appropriate division of credit among a broader data-building community remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines, capabilities and firm-level dynamism has provided a durable alternative framework for understanding technological and organisational change.
assessment.attribution: Winter is centrally identified with the candidate contribution and is the sole credited researcher in this formulation.
assessment.maturity: Its influence has accumulated over decades across innovation, organisational and growth research.
uncertainties: The contribution is closely associated with a wider intellectual tradition, making the boundaries of the prizeable discovery contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on agglomeration, cities and the spatial allocation of activity has transformed understanding of regional growth, housing and urban productivity.
assessment.attribution: Glaeser, Duranton and Moretti represent complementary foundational theoretical and empirical contributions to the modern urban-economics programme.
assessment.maturity: The work is well established, extensively tested and central to policy debates on cities and regional inequality.
uncertainties: Several additional researchers have important claims to credit, particularly on housing and economic geography.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made the distributional consequences of technological change, task displacement and trade shocks empirically legible and economically consequential.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a closely connected body of evidence on labour-demand change and local adjustment.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large subsequent literature and remain salient for interpreting structural transformation.
uncertainties: Separating technology, trade and other local shocks remains empirically demanding.
Lawrence F. Katz also has substantial related claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a powerful quantitative account of how distortions in firm-level resource allocation can generate large productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are key contributors to the formulation and development of this research programme.
assessment.maturity: It has become a standard organising framework for work on development, productivity and institutions.
uncertainties: Inferences about particular distortions from observed revenue productivity remain model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The long-run comparative documentation of crises, debt and default reshaped the historical and policy analysis of financial instability.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are jointly and clearly associated with the central historical database and synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has had sustained influence through successive financial and sovereign-debt episodes.
uncertainties: Some empirical claims derived from historical debt data have been debated, even while the underlying research programme remains influential.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy research on institutions, state capacity and fiscal policy has clarified how political incentives shape long-run development and public finance.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are leading and complementary architects of the listed programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced a broad, durable literature connecting formal political economy with empirical institutional research.
uncertainties: The candidate combines several related themes, and the most distinctive jointly attributable core requires careful specification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their analysis of exhaustible resources, biodiversity and inclusive wealth supplied fundamental tools for assessing prosperity when natural capital is depleted.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are foundational contributors to the economic treatment of intertemporal resource constraints and natural wealth.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical contribution is long established and increasingly relevant as environmental accounting enters policy practice.
uncertainties: Measuring biodiversity and inclusive wealth in operational settings remains incomplete and sensitive to valuation assumptions.
